what: The Medication Schedule helps you take the right medicine at the right time. You add each medicine once, and it builds your daily checklist and a weekly chart.
Tick each dose as you take it. The tool shows what is due now, what was not ticked and when the next dose is. You can print a weekly medication chart for the fridge or for someone you care for.
Reminders can pop up while the page is open, and you can download a calendar file so your phone's own calendar reminds you. Your list stays on this device.
uses: Blood pressure, diabetes or thyroid medicine at the same time every day.

Pick once a day, every 8 hours and so on. The times fill in; change any of them.

In today's checklist, press Take when you take a dose. Press again to undo.

features: Up to 8 times a day, every 4, 6, 8 or 12 hours, or your own times.
Choose the days of the week for weekly medicines.
Due now, not ticked, taken time and next dose.
See the whole week; it starts on your region's first day of the week.
A4 or US Letter, 1 to 4 weeks, with tick boxes and food notes.
Repeating alerts in your phone or computer calendar.
JSON backup and CSV history export.

example.title: Worked example: a 7-day antibiotic
example.text: Sam's doctor prescribes amoxicillin every 8 hours for 7 days. Sam adds it with "Every 8 hours" (6:00, 14:00, 22:00) and an end date 6 days after today. The checklist shows 3 doses a day, the weekly chart stops after the last day, and the calendar file adds 3 repeating alerts that end on that date.

tips: Keep the page open, or use the calendar file, if you rely on reminders.
Tick doses straight after you take them, not later from memory.
Set an end date for short courses so they disappear when finished.
Use the notes for things like "Swallow whole" or "Avoid grapefruit".
Back up your list before changing phones.
